thread.title: Apple: Its Big Event Might Not Be the Market-Mover It Once Was

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: Its Big Event Might Not Be the Market-Mover It Once Was
text:
Photo: courtesy of Apple By David Marino-Nachison Updated Aug. 31, 2018 10:29 a.m. ET Do anything for long enough and it can get stale—no matter how exciting it used to be. Baseball games start to drag. Work in the field of your dreams gets routine. And the announcement of the next Apple (AAPL) event conjures up as much snark as anticipation .
And where, by the way, are our Apple Cars ? (Or, for that matter, our Apple television sets ?)
Anyway, here we are again: Apple’s market capitalization is still around that magical-yet-mundane $1 trillion number, and journalists are flashing invites to what’s expected to be the company’s next big device unveiling on Sept. 12.
Newsletter Sign-up What exactly will happen there isn’t known, which of course is the point of the announcement. Some degree of product announcement, likely including the fall’s iPhone lineup , certainly seems likely, though some observers have suggested that new iPads might be revealed.
And the site 9to5Mac on Thursday published two articles with images of what could be a new iPhone and Apple Watch; they (wisely, perhaps—not that we’d steal) marked up those photos with their logos, so feel free to visit their stories ( Watch , iPhone ) if you’re curious.
Apple didn’t respond to a Thursday email requesting more information about the event and the aforementioned photos. Meantime, the Barron’s Next 50 stock is up more than 30% in 2018, well ahead of the S&P 500.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 In its latest quarter, Apple demonstrated that while it’s still on its way to becoming a services company that also sells devices, its devices are still extremely valuable. A $1,000 price tag is no longer particularly crazy on a phone, and high-end demand has lately helped both Apple and other makers.
“The ongoing expansion of Apple’s ecosystem, along with the global growth of iPhone demand, especially in emerging markets…will continue to drive strong business performance trends,” Tigress Research wrote Thursday while reiterating a “strong buy” rating on the stock.
There’s still concern out there: Teresa Rivas recently noted an analysts’ concern that demand for the iPhone X may eat into enthusiasm for newer models, leading to disappointing sales next year . On Friday, Nomura Instinet analysts estimated FY2019 volumes “essentially flat” with 2018s, with “modestly” rising average selling prices.
”The import once granted the release of the new iPhones” has “lessened,” they wrote. “We expect the impending cycle to bring stable unit volumes, modest ASP expansion, and generally sufficient verve to allow services and buybacks to drive earnings per share growth.”
Or…maybe the disappointment will come much sooner—and the Sept. 12 event will be the Worst. Apple Event. Ever . Start sharpening your hashtags.
